title: Affine-curve cohomological dimension
statement:
Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field, let $C$ be a smooth affine curve over $k$ [def-sc-curves] (separated and of finite type over $k$, of dimension at most one, possibly empty or disconnected), and let $d\geq1$ be prime to $\operatorname{char}k$. Let $\underline{\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z}$ be the constant etale sheaf [def-sc-constant-sheaves], and use etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology]. Then
$$H^q(C_{\Et},\underline{\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z})=0\qquad(q>1).$$
If $C$ is nonempty and connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], then also
$$H^0(C_{\Et},\underline{\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z})\cong\mathbf Z/d\mathbf Z.$$
The latter identification is induced by constant sections. Connectedness is needed only for the degree-zero assertion.

proof.text: Put F = C.constantZMod d. From hd obtain d ≠ 0, and apply the proved Scheme.isTorsion_constantZMod: multiplication by d is zero on the coefficient group, and the additive constant-sheaf functor preserves this identity. Hence every local section is killed by d. IsCurve supplies separatedness, finite type and topological Krull dimension at most one.

Apply torsionEtaleCohomologicalDimensionLE_of_dim_le_one [lem-sc-arbitrary-curve-cd] to f and IsCurve.krullDim_le_one. Its nonaffine alternative contradicts the IsAffine instance. Its affine alternative is exactly the vanishing of the stated derived étale cohomology for every q > 1 and torsion F. Apply it to F from Step 1. This single argument includes the empty, disconnected and zero-dimensional cases. The wrapper uses the source affine-curve bound sk-prop-cd-affine, so the unit route is retained; no general-dimensional affine induction or Kummer computation is needed here.

Assume C is connected. Apply bijective_toSheafify_app_terminal [lem-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf-sections-connected] to the coefficient group A = ULift (ZMod d). This is exactly the unit of constant sheaf adjoint to terminal-object evaluation. Transport along Sheaf.ΓNatIsoSheafSections: Adjunction.unit_rightAdjointUniq_hom_app identifies that unit with the global-sections unit followed by an isomorphism. Cancel the latter to prove that the global-sections unit A → Γ(F) is an isomorphism.

Global sections is additive and preserves finite limits as a right adjoint. The sheaf category is Grothendieck abelian and has enough injectives. Apply the proved rightDerivedSingleUnit_zero [lem-sbc-right-derived-single-zero-unit] to Γ and F. After composing H0 of the canonical single-unit map with homologyRightDerivedFunctorObjSingleFunctorIso followed by rightDerivedZeroIsoSelf, it is the canonical single-homology isomorphism. Cancel this target comparison to conclude that H0 of the single-unit is an isomorphism. Unfold the specified constantZModToDerivedCohomologyZero and combine its last two homology maps with Functor.map_comp: it is precisely the global-sections unit from Step 3, the inverse single-homology comparison, and this H0 single-unit map. Each factor is invertible, proving the specified canonical map is invertible. This argument applies to every connected scheme and requires no dimension-one hypothesis.
